newsitem.title: BULGARIA: POWER CUTS THREATEN BULGARIA THIS WINTER.
newsitem.headline: POWER CUTS THREATEN BULGARIA THIS WINTER.

text.p: Bulgaria may be hit by power cuts this winter if its oldest Soviet-made reactor, which had started safety tests, would not be put on stream in December, National Electricity Company (NEC) chairman said on Wednesday.

Kozma Kuzmanov told Bulgaria's parliamentary energy committee that if the condition of the vessel's metal of reactor number one needs upgrading, the NEC would be forced to delay its restart until the beginning of February.
"In this case we will have to impose (electricity consumption) restrictions," Kuzmanov told the committee.
He said the transportation of the samples of the metal of the reactor's vessel and their analysis at Korchatov's Institute in Russia would last five weeks.
"We hope to receive the preliminary results of the analysis at the beginning of November and if they show the metal is safe we will restart the reactor at the beginning of December," Kuzmanov said.
Westinghouse Electric Corp on Sunday completed procedures of taking metal samples from the 440-megawatt reactor after its closure in May amid international concern over safety.
Kuzmanov said the delay of Westinghouse in taking the samples had caused considerable losses to the NEC.
Fresh fuel will be supplied from Russia for recharging the Kozloduy VVER-1000 reactor number six from 2-5 October and the reactor would be restarted at the beginning of November, he said.
Energy officials said the fuel would be transported by air.
Kozloduy's four 440-megawatt reactors and two 1,000-megawatt reactors produced more than half of the country's electricity.
